subject: The November recruiting report: a new NCAA eligibility rule, and what changed in the standards
preview: What every track family should know this month.
intro: Here's what changed in college track and field recruiting this month, and what it means for your family.

sections.h: In the news: the NCAA's new five-year eligibility rule
sections.html:
In June, the NCAA Division I Cabinet approved an age-based eligibility rule. An athlete's eligibility clock now starts when they enroll in college or at the start of the academic year after they turn 19, whichever comes first. From there they get five seasons in five years, which effectively ends the redshirt year.

What it means for you: the rule applies to athletes who enroll in fall 2027 or later, so it covers today's high school juniors. If your athlete is thinking about a gap year or a postgrad year, the clock may already be running, so check with the NCAA Eligibility Center before you decide. In Runner's World, coaches and recruiters say programs will need to spot talent earlier and develop younger athletes, instead of leaning on runners in their mid-20s. Read the Runner's World story

sections.h: What changed in the standards this month
sections.html:
• Power 4 schools (ACC, Big Ten, Big 12, SEC) no longer show a Walk-On level. These programs keep only a handful of walk-on spots and fill them case by case, so the Recruit mark is the realistic bar.
  • The Big Ten got faster in the hurdles and jumps. The boys' Recruit marks are now 13.70 in the 110m hurdles, 6'10" in the high jump and 49' 7.5" in the triple jump, in high school terms.
  • Sprint and distance levels now come from every conference athlete's season best, not just conference finalists. That made Recruit marks a little more realistic at most Power 4 schools.

College indoor season opens the first weekend of December. For high school athletes, every new mark this winter is a reason to update every coach on your list. Coaches recruit the athletes who keep reaching them with a mark that fits.
A Recruit in the men's 400m needs 46.71 in the Big Ten this year and 45.77 in the SEC.
